Shark Diving Tour

Frequently Asked Questions

Immersion & Interactivity

Our goal is to give guests one of the most immersive and interactive shark diving experiences available — not just a distant look from the boat or a quick swim in the water.

Safety & Experience

Our safety divers and photographers are elite shark divers and true adventurers who have spent thousands of hours working in the water with sharks.

That experience matters. It shows up in how we read shark behavior, keep guests safe and help them to feel comfortable, and create the extraordinary encounters that Hawaii Adventure Diving is known for.

Customer Service

If you read our reviews, you'll see guests call out our crew by name again and again. That's because the care, patience, and attention our team gives each guest is a huge part of the experience.

We take that seriously. It's an honor to share the water with these animals and to help our guests experience sharks in a way that feels safe, personal, unforgettable, and deeply respectful.

Cage-free shark diving is a real open-ocean experience, so safety is always top priority. Our expert shark safety divers are in the water with you, guiding the group, reading shark behavior at all times, and helping guests feel comfortable from start to finish.

You should be comfortable in the water, but you do not need to be an expert swimmer. Guests wear snorkel gear and remain under the guidance of our crew during the experience.

If you are a stronger swimmer, you may be able to move more comfortably in the water and get better photo opportunities. If you are less confident, our crew can help you settle in and enjoy the experience at a pace that feels right for you.

No. This is not a scuba diving tour. It is a cage-free shark snorkeling experience in the open ocean.

You do not need scuba certification or diving experience. We provide the basic snorkel gear and guide you through what to expect before you enter the water.

No. This is not a scuba diving tour. It is a cage-free shark snorkeling experience in the open ocean.

You do not need scuba certification or diving experience. We provide the basic snorkel gear and guide you through what to expect before you enter the water.

Many tours feature Galapagos sharks — powerful, beautiful open-ocean sharks that are often around 6 to 8 feet long. Depending on conditions and the day's wildlife, you may also see sandbar sharks, silky sharks, hammerheads, or on rare occassions, the tiger shark.

No specific species can be guaranteed, and that is part of the adventure. These are wild sharks in the open ocean, so every encounter is different.

A typical shark tour consists of taking the boat out to the dive site, which is about 3 miles off the coast of the North Shore of Oahu, followed by swimming with sharks, and then the trip back to the dock. The entire tour takes about 2 hours from start to finish.

Ocean conditions can vary, and some guests are more sensitive to motion than others. If you are prone to seasickness, we recommend taking motion sickness medication before the tour according to the directions on the label or advice from your doctor.

Our crew is used to helping first-time guests feel comfortable, and being prepared ahead of time can make the whole experience much more enjoyable. If you are unsure, it is better to plan for it than wish you had.

We recommend bringing:

  • light jacket, sunglasses, and a hat
  • sunscreen (reef-safe if possible)
  • towel
  • a change of clothes if you'd prefer to be dry on that ride back to the dock

Try to pack light and arrive ready for the water. If you think you might get motion sickness, plan ahead before the tour.

Snorkel gear is provided, however you're welcome to bring your own if you prefer.

Feel to bring a waterproof camera like a GoPro to capture your own photos and video as well.
